title: Dijkstra's Shortest Paths
hints: Repeatedly finalise the closest unvisited node.
Build adjacency lists, keep distances as `Int?`, and relax each neighbour of the chosen node.
jsBridge: The same algorithm as in JS, but Swift's standard library has no priority queue (JS has none either). The O(V²) version with a `visited` array is fine for small graphs, and `Int?` distances make "unreachable" explicit instead of `Infinity`.

compass.q: JS uses `Infinity` for unreachable distances. What does `[Int?]` force you to handle that `Infinity` hides?
O(V²) array scan vs a binary heap (swift-collections `Heap`): at what graph size does the heap win?
Why does Dijkstra break with negative edge weights? What would you use instead?
Routing in MapKit is done for you (`MKDirections`). When would an app still run its own shortest path (games, indoor maps)?
